text:
anya: FYI I kicked off a quant bakeoff for llamaX-13B (FP16 baseline, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) focused on function-calling / structured JSON output.
anya: Short summary: AWQ shows a spike in tool-args/JSON validity failures vs GPTQ and FP8. numbers below.
eval-bot: run 2025-11-17T10:02Z completed. workloads: tool-calls-v2 (2000 samples).
eval-bot: results: FP16 99.4% json_valid, FP8 98.9%, GPTQ 98.6%, AWQ 93.1% json_valid.
miguel: ouch. is that overall json schema invalid or specific key drift?
anya: mostly schema-valid but tool_args missing/typed wrong or arrays collapsed into string for certain calls. example below.
anya: ```json
expected: {"tool_name":"search","tool_args":{"query":"weather in SF","max_results":5}}
awq_out: {"tool_name":"search","tool_args":"{\"query\": \"weather in SF\", \"max_results\":5}"}
```
kai: interesting — AWQ seems to be serializing the args into a string in ~3% of failures. could be tokenizer/decoder config or beam vs greedy sampling.
jen: any correlation with temperature or sampling? was this deterministic sampling during eval?
anya: eval used greedy for function-calling eval, temp=0.0. same decode codepath across quant types.
miguel: is it possible AWQ's int8 packing changed token boundaries for certain punctuation which triggers the model to output a quoted JSON blob?
jen: maybe. also check tokenizer fast vs slow differences.
anya: I scanned examples. pattern: when nested dicts have numbers or booleans, AWQ sometimes emits double-encoded JSON inside tool_args. count is ~3.5% of samples, but those are high-severity because tool parser rejects them.
anya: reproduction snippet:```bash
# reproduce single sample run
python eval_tool_call.py --model llamaX-13B-awq-q4 --sample-id 1372 --decode greedy --seed 42
# output saved to /tmp/awq-1372.json
```
miguel: can you dump logits or raw tokens around the region? need to see if model produced a quotation mark token before the brace.
anya: attached: token trace for sample 1372 (trimmed).
anya: TOKEN_TRACE: [..., 259, 34, 123, 34, 113, ...] // 34 = '"', 123 = '{'
kai: that looks like it inserted a leading quote then an encoded blob.
jen: any config differences in generation libs used for AWQ binary? same transformer/llama.cpp interface?
anya: we used our standard runner for all models. AWQ was loaded with awq_runtime v0.9. injector flags: --kv-cache true --decode-impl "fast".
miguel: try forcing decode-impl to "baseline" for AWQ and rerun a small batch. if passes then it's runtime decode bug.
jen: also try toggling the tokenizer option "add_prefix_space" and check for byte-level tokenization quirks.
anya: will run two quick checks: 1) decode-impl baseline, 2) tokenizer fast->slow. scheduling now. ETA ~30m.
eval-bot: quick delta run queued.
[~20 minutes later]
anya: quick results: decode-impl baseline: AWQ json_valid -> 96.8% (big improvement). tokenizer slow: AWQ json_valid -> 95.2%. both together -> 97.1%.
miguel: so both factors matter but decode impl biggest impact. suggests decoder postprocessing in fast path is collapsing braces into string occasionally.
jen: can you capture raw bytes and compare the exact token spans for fast vs baseline? want to see if tokenization differences propagate or if the fast decoder stitches tokens wrongly.
anya: grabbing diffs now, will push to /tmp/awq-diffs-176820.
kai: for deployment risk: AWQ still cheaper but if tool-call reliability drops we might need fallback routing by route. suggest routing function-calling traffic to GPTQ or FP8 for now, or enable post-parse fixups.
jen: post-parse fixup like attempt json.loads if tool_args is string and then re-parse? that could work as temporary mitigation. add warning logs and a metric for "tool_args_double_encoded".
miguel: agreed. also raise a bug with awq-runtime upstream: include token traces and sample ids. I'll take that.
anya: I'll open GH issue, attach sample tokens, and add a canary rollout plan.
deploy-bot: canary plan proposed: route 10% of function-call traffic to AWQ with post-parse fix enabled, 90% to GPTQ. monitor json_valid_rate and latency for 1 hour.
enj: typo on the bot name :P
jen: ack :)
anya: created issue https://github.com/redwood/awq-runtime/issues/452 with sample and tokens. putting a temporary eval-run in the pipeline to re-run at scale overnight.
miguel: thanks. next steps: (1) quick fixup in runner (2) small canary routing (3) open upstream issue. sounds good.
anya: yup. I'll follow up with numbers after the overnight job. :thumbsup:
